text:
maya: Quick question — when someone switches from a per-route view to the per-model tab in Console analytics, should we try to preserve the active filters & saved query context or treat it as a fresh model-centric view?

alex: My vote is preserve most filters (time range, query text, tag filters) but drop route-scoped routing pins (region/capacity) that don't make sense at model level.

samira: +1 to preserve. Users expect continuity when they click between tabs. Losing time range is the worst.

ken: Preserve sounds good but we need to be explicit about quotas/preview cost. If route had a quota override, switching to model view should surface that it's not applied. Maybe a banner: "You are viewing model metrics; route-specific quotas not applied".

maya: Agree on the banner. Also product asked if saved queries should be scoped to route, model, or both. Current backend saves saved_query.scope = "route" | "model" | "global"... Is that fine or too coarse?

priya: The coarse scope is ok but we need a merging rule. UI should show both matching saved queries when in combined context. E.g., in route view show route-specific + global. In model view show model-specific + global. In combined route+model view show route-model specific if exists else suggest global/model ones.

alex: Implementation note: saved_query payload we get from api is small, e.g. 
```
{
  "id": "sq_123",
  "scope": "route", // route|model|global
  "filters": ["time:7d","model:mosaic-v2","route:photos-api"],
}
```
We could add inferred_scope_labels in UI rather than change API. Keep API stable.

ken: Telemetry question: when a user applies a saved query, do we need to emit separate events for 'applied-from-route' vs 'applied-from-model' so we can track discoverability?

samira: Yes, please. We already struggle to know whether people discover saved queries via route page or model page. Add event: analytics.saved_query_applied { saved_query_id, origin: "route"|"model"|"global", applied_filters_count }.

maya: Good call. Also about rollouts — if we preserve model filter we must be careful with rollout comparisons. E.g., route-level A/B rollout pinned to variant-a vs variant-b; the model view should not accidentally compare rollout groups. Suggest: special-case rollout filters and show them as disabled with explanation when switching scopes.

priya: UX microcopy: "Rollout filters are route-scoped and are not applied in model view. See route tab to compare rollout groups." Add a small link to open route tab with same time range and model filter.

alex: Syncing behavior: clicking the banner should offer a one-click jump back to original route view with preserved filters. That should reuse existing deep-linking API: /console/route/{routeId}?q={encodedFilters}&t={time}. We already have route deep links.

ken: Edge case — what if model tab doesn't support some complex predicates (e.g., per-token cost buckets or hardware tags)? We should drop unsupported filters and show which ones were dropped. Telemetry: log dropped_filters_count and names.

maya: OK next steps: Alex to add inferred_scope_labels in UI and banner flow; Samira to add telemetry events; Priya to craft copy and deep-link behaviour; Ken to add guardrails for rollout/unsupported filters. I'll collect and write a short RFC for eng-runtime and product so we can align on API stability.

deploy-bot: Reminder: canary rollout for console changes deploys tomorrow 07:30 PT — flag: preserve-filter-pivot. If you need to opt out, reply here.

maya: Thanks — I'll draft the RFC today and ping infra about telemetry quotas for the new events.

samira: I'll add tests for event shape in telemetry repo and wire up kinesis schema.

alex: I'll prototype UI labels this afternoon and link to Maya's RFC.

priya: I'll write copy for the banner and the tooltip for dropped filters.

ken: Filed a small infra ticket to add rollout-filter metadata check: infra#4572.

maya: Great, closing loop — will follow up with RFC link in this thread once it's done.
